notes: δικαίου → 'a righteous man' and τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ → 'the ... man' / 'good' are analysed differently only because one is anarthrous and the other articular, which is the test rules 51, 58 and 102 use: the anarthrous phrase heads on the adjective, the articular one gives the determiner and the supplied nominal to the article headed on 'man'.
The infinitival 'to' of 'to die' is the verb's own helper, no conjunction governing the clause (rules 7 and 40).
